reason: Rules the generated NPC conversations and the shop window follow where MeowDB is silent. Until Iteration Three they lived only in code (audit: quests and npcs_shops domains); they are recorded here so the provenance audit sees them. NpcDialogueBuilder reads offer_prompt and default_talk, ShopWindow reads shop_window_title, and NpcDialogueBuilder.validate_rules() fails on a value the code does not implement, so this file cannot drift from the behaviour.

offer_prompt.reason: MeowDB lists a quest's "On accept" lines in order without marking which one asks the question. MisoStory shows them as pages and puts Yes/No under the last one. For most quests the last line is a question (1006: "...want me to train you?"); for 1000 it is the Quest Helper tip and for 1014-1019 it is "talk to me when you're ready for the next question", statements kept as the prompt because writing a question would invent NPC speech. A quest with no On accept text (1002) is offered as a quest card with the system offer_prompt instead (_system.json).

in_progress_lines.reason: Sera's "Did you give my mirror to Heena? When will she help me with the laundry..." asks about the mirror she hands over in 1001 (Bringing a Mirror to Heena), so it shows only while 1001 is in progress; before and after it she says line 0 ("It's a fine day for laundry, don't you think?"). While 1001 is in progress her conversation opens on the canonical reminder (1001's wrong_npc branch) or the lost-mirror branch, so her default talk is reached only when neither shows.

Sen's "What did my sister say? Oh, I'm so hungry..." waits for Nina's answer, which the player carries in 1004 (Returning to Nina), so it shows only while 1004 is in progress; before and after it he says line 0 ("There's nothing to eat in here. Oh...").

default_talk.in_progress_lines_reason: Per-NPC overrides of quest_npc: each row's line (0-based, the NPC's "What X Says" lines) shows only while its quest is in progress, and otherwise the NPC's other lines follow the general rule. NpcDialogueBuilder.validate_rules() fails on a row whose NPC, line or quest does not exist.
default_talk.reason: MeowDB does not label when each "What X Says" line is shown (docs/canonical/npcs.md, gaps). Quest NPCs with two or more lines say line 0 until every quest they start or end is completed, then the last line, which reads as the after-quest line for Heena, Roger, Maria, Rain and Mai. Sera's "Did you give my mirror to Heena?" and Sen's "What did my sister say?" read as mid-quest lines, so by the owner's ruling (#9) each shows only while the quest it refers to is in progress (in_progress_lines). quest_npc may also be "all_lines_in_order". Townsfolk say all their lines as pages; an NPC with no quoted lines says its first speech-bubble line.

quiz.reason: MeowDB pairs no rule with Rain's quizzes: it does not say whether a wrong answer may be retried (1015's text suggests it can) or whether the next quiz follows at once. A wrong answer shows its paired canonical wrong-answer line and ends the chat with the quest still in progress (talk again to retry); after a right answer the next quiz is offered in a new conversation. Recorded only: the code has this one behaviour.

shop_window_title.reason: MeowDB has no shop title. The shop window names the shopkeeper ("Lucy's Shop") with the canonical function title and map under it; {npc} is the canonical NPC name.
